content:
mike: Seeing a repeat of noisy neighbor on eu-west-2 last night, but weird: NIC interrupt storms correlate with egress bridge flow >100k pps. Any ideas?
elaine: Yup saw alerts. Packet drops on sidecar + host tx queue spikes. Metrics: host_net_tx_dropped spike ~1200, gpu-serving latency +80ms.
sam: Do we have recorded `ethtool` settings? IRQ coalescing maybe changed after the kernel update.
infra-bot: Alert: net-irq-high on rack-9-eu2 at 2026-03-18T02:15Z
ben: Quick workaround: reduce NIC coalescing rx-usecs to 50 and tx-usecs 50 on affected hosts. Command: `ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 50 tx-usecs 50`
elaine: Tried that on 3 hosts, CPU irq balanced better, but observed CPU steal on multi-tenant hosts. Looks like NIC steering increased interrupt rate -> more CPU contention with GPU processing threads.
mike: Could we push a routing policy to prefer dedicated pools for tenants hitting >500 RPS or long sequences? Route fallback to dedicated when egress pps crosses threshold.
sam: Problem: our router has no visibility into NIC-level telemetry. We only see per-node egress pps. Need a small probe agent to emit per-nic pps and irq_rate so routing can make informed decisions.
ben: Alternatively we can implement an egress-bridge shim that aggregates flows and enforces shaping per-tenant at the host. Low-effort example using tc/iptables:
```
# create HTB root and two classes
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 12
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 10gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:12 htb rate 9gbit ceil 10gbit
# attach filter by fwmark set by iptables
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -m mark --mark 0x1 -j MARK --set-mark 1
```
ben: This offloads shaping to kernel tc but still cheap CPU.
elaine: iptables on hot path still hurts. Prefer NIC offload + hardware TC where possible. Also need to watch tail latency for short chat flows.
mike: Cost note: dedicated pools are ~2.3x more expensive but reduce tail latency significantly. We have an enterprise customer already seeing regressions. Need a decision by EOD for a targeted mitigation.
sam: I'll prototype the per-nic probe + a scheduler rule: if irq_rate > 10k/sec and egress_pps > 100k then mark node `bridge-congested` and route new allocations to other AZs or dedicated slices.
ben: Add graceful fallback: canary migrate long-running sequences for 30s and monitor KV cache warmup cost and delta in per-token cost.
elaine: Also add telemetry: track kvcache_hit_ratio and migration churn so we don't trade latency for huge cache misses.
mike: SGTM. Sam, can you write a short RFC with rollout, telemetry, and rollback playbook? Keep it minimal.
sam: Will post RFC in #eng-infra by lunchtime. For now toggling ethtool changes as a stopgap on 6 nodes and watching.
infra-bot: Deploy job mike/patch/irq-coalesce started
ben: :thumbsup:
